required_outcomes: Records that the landlord is arranging the works through his own contractor (Riverside Services) and paying them directly, quoting his email.
Does not instruct or assign an agency contractor and does not seek spend approval as if the agency were placing the order.
Puts the request on hold waiting for the landlord (or sets a dated follow-up) with a short review date and a specific ask: Riverside's go-ahead and start date.
Tells the tenant that the landlord has seen the report and is arranging his own contractor, without inventing a visit or start date.
acceptable_alternatives: Asking the landlord for Freya's contact details or the expected timescale, as long as the request still waits on the landlord rather than on an agency contractor.
Leaving the tenant update until the landlord confirms a date, provided a dated follow-up is set and recorded.
positive_behaviours: Passes the access points from the tenant's answers (one cat at the property, the path access to the back properties) to the landlord for his contractor.
Notes that the tenant said the side strip was promised last summer, so the landlord knows this is a repeat report.
red_flags: Escalating to a human when the landlord has given a clear instruction for a routine communal job.
Asking the landlord to approve a spend limit or a quote for agency works.
prohibited_actions: Assigning an agency contractor or raising an agency works order for the garden.
Approving any quote or payment through the agency.
critical_failures: Instructing an agency contractor to do the garden works against the landlord's written instruction not to.
